actions.action: Rinse leaves with lukewarm water in the shower to remove sulphur residue
Remove leaves that are more than half brown
Spray insecticidal soap or spinosad every 5-7 days for 4 weeks, covering undersides and moss pole, in the evening
Optionally release predatory mites (Amblyseius cucumeris) once sulphur is gone
Slide plant out of pot and check roots for rot
If roots are rotten, trim them and repot into chunky mix of soil, bark and perlite
Check that the top 3-4 cm of soil is dry before watering
Move plant to 1-1.5 m from the window, out of direct afternoon sun
Prune bare vines back to just above a node
Root the cuttings as a backup plant

reason: The answer blames sulphur burn and casts thrips and low light as background or alternative causes (partial), but its fix still treats thrips, prunes and propagates cuttings, and moves the plant closer to light, matching what worked, with nothing likely to harm the plant.
